full_text_en:
Hangzhou Wahaha Group Corporation v. Zhuhai Giant High-Tech Group Corporation — dispute over unfair competition

Plaintiff: Hangzhou Wahaha Group Corporation

Legal Representative: Zong Qinghou, Chairman and General Manager

Agent ad litem: Hu Jianmiao and Li Yongming, lawyers from Huaxia Law Firm, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province

Defendant: Zhuhai Giant High-Tech Group Corporation

Legal Representative: Shi Yuzhu, Chairman and General Manager

Agent ad litem: Wang Jian, Chief Administrative Officer of the Corporation

Plaintiff Hangzhou Wahaha Group Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Wahaha Group) filed an action with the Intermediate People's Court of Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, on the grounds that Defendant Zhuhai Giant High-Tech Group Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Giant Group) had engaged in unfair competition.

Plaintiff's Allegations: "Wahaha Children's Nutritional Liquid" is a product developed and produced by our company. Its advertising slogan "Drink Wahaha, and meals taste great" has become a household phrase. This product has won more than twenty major awards, including the National Most Popular Health Product, the Second Prize of the National Spark Award, and the Gold Medal for Chinese High-Quality Health Products. In recent years, sales have maintained a leading position among similar domestic products. The plaintiff has also enjoyed high commercial reputation and product reputation both domestically and internationally due to this product. In early 1995, Defendant Giant Group produced a product similar to "Wahaha Children's Nutritional Liquid", named "Giant Eat Delicious", which was launched on the national market. Giant Group specially printed a promotional booklet titled "Giant Group Health Products Sales Brochure: Giant's Big Campaign", widely distributed to food and pharmaceutical sales units and consumers nationwide. The promotional booklet stated: "It is rumored that Wahaha contains hormones, causing children to mature early and giving rise to many modern childhood diseases." Consequently, distributors and consumers of Wahaha products nationwide demanded an explanation from the plaintiff. This conduct of the defendant caused a decline in sales of Wahaha Children's Nutritional Liquid nationwide, resulting in the first negative growth since the product was launched in 1987. Even sales in Hangzhou, the plaintiff's home base, could not escape this misfortune. As of December 31, 1995, the plaintiff suffered a decrease in sales revenue of RMB 44,929,200 and direct economic losses of RMB 6,739,380. More seriously, the plaintiff's good commercial reputation, product reputation, and corporate image were severely damaged. The defendant's conduct constitutes unfair competition and infringes upon the plaintiff's legitimate rights and interests. Therefore, the plaintiff requests the court to order the defendant to immediately cease the unfair competition acts that damage the plaintiff's commercial reputation and product reputation; to order the defendant to pay RMB 6,739,380 in direct economic losses and RMB 3,200,000 in compensation for reputational damage; and to order the defendant to publicly apologize, restore the plaintiff's reputation, and bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant Giant Group did not submit a written defense.

The Intermediate People's Court of Hangzhou found the following facts upon trial: The plaintiff's product "Wahaha Children's Nutritional Liquid" was tested and proven not to have the issue of "containing hormones, causing children to mature early, and giving rise to many modern childhood diseases". The plaintiff provided sufficient evidence, and the alleged facts were confirmed upon investigation.

The Intermediate People's Court of Hangzhou held that Article 14 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC provides: "Business operators shall not fabricate or disseminate false facts to damage the commercial reputation or product reputation of competitors." The defendant's dissemination of false facts to damage the plaintiff's product reputation constitutes an act of unfair competition. Pursuant to Article 20 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the defendant shall bear tort liability for damages and shall also bear the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff in investigating its unfair competition act. Accordingly, the Intermediate People's Court of Hangzhou, in accordance with Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, presided over mediation on the basis of finding the facts and distinguishing right from wrong. The defendant expressed its intention to reflect on its tortious acts and to take them as a lesson. The plaintiff accepted the defendant's attitude. Under the court's auspices, the parties reached the following mediation agreement on October 7, 1996:

1. Defendant Giant Group acknowledges that it engaged in unfair competition acts, causing damage to the commercial reputation and product reputation of Plaintiff Wahaha Group, and is willing to bear corresponding legal liability.

2. Giant Group ceases its unfair competition acts. After the conclusion of this case, Giant Group will apologize to Wahaha Group and eliminate the adverse effects through a joint press conference. The specific time and method will be separately agreed upon by both parties.

3. Giant Group shall compensate Wahaha Group for direct economic losses of RMB 2,000,000, to be offset by real estate of equivalent value. Specific procedures shall be handled by both parties in accordance with relevant regulations.

4. The above sum shall be paid by Giant Group to Wahaha Group on October 10, 1996. Giant Group shall reimburse Wahaha Group other expenses of RMB 190,340.

5. Wahaha Group waives its other claims.

Case acceptance fee of RMB 59,660 shall be borne by Giant Group.

On January 2, 1997, Giant Group and Wahaha Group jointly held a press conference in Hangzhou, at which Giant Group publicly apologized to Wahaha Group and fulfilled its obligation under the mediation agreement to compensate Wahaha Group for economic losses.
